name: Pisces
introduction: is the Fishes, two fish tied together by a long cord, said to be Aphrodite and Eros escaping the monster Typhon. It is a large but faint zodiac constellation, best seen on northern autumn evenings. One of its fish is marked by a ring of stars called the Circlet.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Today, the Sun crosses the celestial equator into the northern sky at the March equinox in Pisces. Earth’s slowly wobbling axis has moved this point from Aries into Pisces, and it is now drifting toward Aquarius.

[Van Maanen’s Star](id:10pc-0073), about 14 light-years away, is the nearest solitary white dwarf. In 1917, it became the first star found with metals on its surface, which we now know are debris from shattered planets falling onto it.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Alrescha](hip:9487), “the cord”, marks the knot that ties the fish together; it is a binary of two white stars. [Alpherg](hip:7097) is the brightest star, a yellow giant.
The Circlet includes [Gamma Piscium](hip:114971), [Iota Piscium](hip:116771) and [Omega Piscium](hip:118268) at its edge.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: The millisecond pulsar [PSR J0030+0451](id:psr-j0030p0451) was the first neutron star whose surface hot spots were mapped by NASA’s NICER. Galaxies include M74, the Phantom Galaxy, a face-on spiral.
